note: The class-keyed combat opener of `orig/g.exe`: the half-open image range `1000:3d32`..`1000:3e8d`, entered only from `FUN_1000_3d11`'s `param_1` gate and mapped by Task 39 from an aligned decode, never from a screen. Prose twin: `docs/re/combat-opener.md`; re-derived from `orig/g.exe` by `tools/test_combat_opener.py`. `data/gym_arms.json` is the shape this follows. COVERAGE BOUNDARY: this artifact covers exactly that range and nothing else -- not the `param_1` 1/3/4 arms that follow it at `1000:3e8d`, `1000:3ead` and `1000:3f2b`, and not `1000:3fa7`, the blow-budget block the exit jumps to. The sweeps in `tools/test_combat_opener.py` (literals, branches, draws, absolute reads and writes, span tiling, entries, exits) are SET EQUALITIES over the range, so an omitted entry reds the test.
address_forms: `1000:xxxx` is a Ghidra label (Form A of `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`) and, because the game's code segment is the load base, its OFF is also the image offset. `20ae:xxxx` is DGROUP. `0eed:` and `0f78:` are Form B runtime segments. `cs_offset` is the image offset of a Pascal shortstring's LENGTH byte -- the exact immediate of the `mov di,imm16` that pushes it -- and `file_offset` is that plus the 0x18d0-byte MZ header, which is what `data/strings.json` keys on.

range.note: Half-open. `1000:3d32` IS the `mov ax,[0x3952]` that loads the key; `1000:3e8d` is the `param_1 == 1` compare and is NOT part of this map. The 168-instruction count is `docs/re/gaps.md`'s, re-measured here from an aligned walk that tiles the range with no gap and no overlap.

entered_by.claim: Exactly two branches image-wide target any address in `[1000:3d32, 1000:3e8d)` from outside it, and both target the range's first instruction. `1000:3d24 mov al,[bp+0x4]` is the FUNCTION PARAMETER, not the enemy class: `param_1` 0 and 6 reach the opener and everything else takes `1000:3d2f jmp 0x3e8d`.
entered_by.inherited_from: docs/re/gaps.md, 'the arm 0 and 6 actually take is 1000:3d32..1000:3e8d'. VERIFIED here, not inherited: the entry-site sweep and the 168-instruction walk both reproduce it. The one wording this map corrects is 'classes 0 and 6' -- 0 and 6 are `param_1` values; the CLASSES this chain keys on are the ten `[0x3952]` values below.

exit.claim: `1000:3e8a jmp 0x3fa7` is the ONLY control transfer out of the range: every other branch and jump inside it targets an address inside it. Five arms jump to it (`1000:3d76`, `1000:3dbf`, `1000:3de0`, `1000:3e33`) or fall into it (arm 9, and the silent default via `1000:3e38 jnz 0x3e8a`).
exit.inherited_from: docs/re/gaps.md, 'whose only exit is 1000:3e8a jmp 0x3fa7'. VERIFIED here by decoding every transfer in the range.

key.what: the ROLLED ENEMY's class -- record offset +0x00, `.SAV` 0x200, the rank/class name index (docs/re/combat.md's fighter-record table)

xrefs.note: All four references inside `FUN_1000_3d11` are LOADS; not one of the function's 45 accepted references writes it. The writers are `FUN_1000_0d14` (the wander's enemy generator, clamped to 9 at 1000:0da1) and `FUN_1000_11c2` (1000:11d0 `mov word [0x3952],0xa`, the rector).

arms.name: arm_0_1_2
arms.note: Two plain WriteLn lines. `1000:3d42 jnz 0x3d79` is the only one of the three gates that leaves the arm; 0 and 1 fall in through their own `jz`.

arms.name: arm_3_4_5_6
arms.note: The widest arm: four class values, two plain lines. Class 6 is the LAST link, `1000:3d8b jnz 0x3dc2`.

arms.name: arm_8

fills.what: `lea di,[bp-0x218]`, the STACK local the line is built in -- pushed with `push ss`, not `push ds`
rtl_str_append: += the player's name at 20ae:379c (pushed at 1000:3df8)

rtl_str_append: += ranks[[0x389c]] -- 1000:3e0c loads the PLAYER's class, 1000:3e10/1000:3e12 shift it by 8 and 1000:3e14 adds 0x2e, which is the DS:002e 256-byte-stride table data/string_tables.json carries

arms.note: The enemy recognises the player by name and rank. The `call 0eed:01c2` at 1000:3e2e has no visible string push because rtl_str_assign / rtl_str_append return with `retf 0x4`: each pops only its SOURCE and leaves the destination far pointer on the stack for WriteLn's `retf 0xe` (docs/re/den.md).

arms.name: arm_9

fills.what: `lea di,[bp-0x218]`, the same stack local arm 8 uses
rtl_str_append: += ranks[[0x389c]] -- 1000:3e63 loads the PLAYER's class, 1000:3e67/1000:3e69 shift and 1000:3e6b adds 0x2e

arms.note: Two lines: a plain WriteLn first, then the composed one. This arm does NOT jump to the exit -- it falls into it.

arms.name: arm_default_silent
arms.note: `1000:3e38 jnz 0x3e8a` is the chain's last miss, so any value of [0x3952] the ten compares do not name reaches the exit having printed NOTHING. Such a value is written: 1000:11d0 `mov word [0x3952],0xa` in FUN_1000_11c2 stores 10, the Ректор НГУ row of data/string_tables.json's `ranks`, while the wander's own generator FUN_1000_0d14 clamps its roll at 9 (1000:0d9a `cmp word [0x3952],0x9` / 1000:0d9f `jle` / 1000:0da1 `mov word [0x3952],0x9`). WHETHER THIS ARM EVER RUNS IS NOT ESTABLISHED: it also needs a call whose param_1 is 0 or 6 while the word still holds that value, and the two rector fights docs/re/combat-dispatch.md names pass kinds 3 and 4 (1000:ae2d, 1000:ae39), which take 1000:3d2f jmp 0x3e8d and never enter this range. Recorded as open, not resolved by symmetry.

class_map_note: TEN class values, SIX arms. The brief's phrase 'ten class arms' counts the ten `cmp ax,N` links; five of them print, and the eleventh case -- everything the chain does not name -- prints nothing at all.

globals.name: player name
globals.note: `1000:3df8 mov di,0x379c` loads an IMMEDIATE DGROUP offset, pushed with `push ds` at 1000:3dfb so rtl_str_append can read the string. It is not an absolute-memory operand and so is not in the absolute-read sweep; conflating the two kinds is how a read census over-counts.

spans_note: The eleven spans tile `1000:3d32`..`1000:3e8d` end to end with no gap and no overlap, so a block cannot be dropped from the map by being left out of every span. Each arm's own gates are a separate span from its body because the gates for classes 0..2 sit BEFORE the first body while every later arm's gates sit after the previous body -- the chain is not laid out symmetrically.

sweeps.note: Measured over the half-open range `1000:3d32`..`1000:3e8d` by an aligned walk from `FUN_1000_3d11`'s own entry. `tools/test_combat_opener.py` recomputes every one of these and asserts SET EQUALITY against the records above, so a number here that stopped being true reds the test.
sweeps.random_call_sites_note: A zero proves nothing on its own, so the same `9a 4b 11 78 0f` signature is swept over the WHOLE image in the test and required to find 86 -- the population docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md records. Without that second half this would be the check that cannot fail.
sweeps.memory_operand_note: Only five instructions in the range name memory at all: 1000:3d32, 1000:3e0c and 1000:3e63 READ an absolute DGROUP word, and 1000:3de8 / 1000:3e53 are `lea` -- address arithmetic, not an access. There is no `stos`, no `movs`, no `rep` and no write through a register operand.

no_store_finding.claim: The opener writes NO game state. Not one instruction in `1000:3d32`..`1000:3e8d` writes an absolute DGROUP address, and the only memory the two shortstring helpers write is the STACK local at `ss:[bp-0x218]` (`1000:3de8` / `1000:3e53` push `ss`, not `ds`).
no_store_finding.why_it_needed_saying: docs/re/gaps.md and docs/re/combat.md had established the zero-DRAW claim (no `9a 4b 11 78 0f` in the range) and said nothing about stores. A block that spends no draw can still move the save file; this sweep is what rules that out.
no_store_finding.consequence: Porting the opener cannot change a single byte of state or a single RNG draw: it is print-only, so `tests/combat_sequence.rs` and the five frozen oracles are unaffected by it.

branch_census.note: `data/branches.json` records ten `class == "game"` branches in the range and all ten were `port_touched: false` when Task 39 mapped it. Recompute with the block under 'Recomputation, from the shipped artifacts -> Coverage' in docs/re/branches.md, filtered to `func_entry == "1000:3d11"`.

ds_field_note: `arms[].ds_operands` and `arms[].ds_pointer_pushes` are DIFFERENT SETS and are kept apart because one revision of this file conflated them: a single `ds_pointer_pushes` array held two `mov di,...` operands and one `push ds`, three entries in all, which matched `sweeps.ds_pointer_pushes` by coincidence and so read as cross-checked by it while sharing exactly one address with it. `ds_operands` is the `mov di` that ADDRESSES DGROUP (an immediate offset at 1000:3df8, an absolute read at 1000:3e0c and 1000:3e63); `ds_pointer_pushes` is the `push ds` that supplies the segment half of the far pointer (1000:3dfb, 1000:3e18, 1000:3e6f). `tools/test_combat_opener.py` now requires the union of the arms' `ds_pointer_pushes` to EQUAL the swept `push ds` set, so the two are related by a measurement instead of by a matching cardinality.
